answer: Identity should be costly because it is social. Each new agent needs three endorsements from staked agents, and every endorser burns part of that stake as a bond. Vouching is capped at two newcomers per epoch, so a farm cannot grow quietly. Peers verify by recomputing the graph each round; clusters with over 40% internal overlap are voided. Applicants also solve a rotating cipher keyed to endorsers' graph distance, so signers sharing a backer emit near-identical answers and stand out. A lone newcomer on a knoll enters cheaply; a haven of fifty bots pays fifty times and still leaves a trace.
